problem: A hotel's laundry cart holds 23 bath mats and 39 pillowcases. How many pieces of laundry are in the cart?
follow_up_questions: The housekeeper carries 17 pieces up to the rooms. How many pieces are still in the cart?

problem: What is the total number of things in the camp's lost-and-found bin, which holds 23 water bottles along with 39 hats?
follow_up_questions: Campers claim 17 of the things. How many are left in the bin?

problem: Amara's garden hose is 58 metres long, while Tomas has one of 31 metres. By how many metres is Amara's hose longer?
follow_up_questions: Tomas joins an extra 20 metres onto his hose. How much shorter than Amara's is it now?

problem: How much longer is the red climbing rope than the blue one? At the climbing gym, the red rope measures 58 metres and the blue rope 31 metres.
follow_up_questions: A coach clips 20 more metres onto the blue rope. By how many metres is it still shorter than the red one?

problem: Kofi keeps 35 marbles in a jar. 21 of them are green, 6 are striped, and all the others are clear. How many clear marbles are in the jar?
follow_up_questions: In a playground game, every clear marble counts for 3 points. How many points are his clear marbles worth?

problem: How many tulips does the florist have? Her bucket holds 35 flowers: 21 roses, 6 daisies, and tulips make up the rest.
follow_up_questions: She sells each tulip for 3 dollars. How much money will the tulips bring in?

problem: Ayumi splits her 63 seashells into two boxes, one for spiral shells and one for flat shells. There are 28 spiral shells. Her box lids are painted with dolphins. How many flat shells are there?
How many books are on the fiction cart? The librarian divides 63 returned books between a fiction cart and a science cart, and the science cart gets 28. The carts squeak loudly in the hallway.
Darius got 5 baskets in the netball drill, and Priya got 9. How many more baskets did Priya get than Darius?
follow_up_questions: What was their combined number of baskets?

problem: In a spelling bee, how many more words did Ingrid spell right than Pablo? Ingrid managed 9 words and Pablo 5.
follow_up_questions: Together, how many words did the two of them spell right?

problem: Selma wants a 25 metre fence along her vegetable patch. She has put up 17 metres so far. How much more fence does she need?
follow_up_questions: The fence comes in panels that are 2 metres long. How many panels does she need?
A panel costs 3 dollars. What will the panels cost her?

problem: How many metres of the school fair banner are still unpainted, if the banner should be 25 metres long and the children have painted 17 metres?
follow_up_questions: They paint the rest in strips of 2 metres each. How many strips must they paint?
Paint for one strip costs 3 dollars. How much does the paint for those strips cost?

problem: Mr. Haddad looks after the fish tanks in 2 classrooms. There are 24 fish in the red room's tank and 39 in the blue room's tank. How many more fish are in the blue room's tank?
follow_up_questions: He moves 9 fish from the blue room's tank to the red room's tank. How many fish are in the red room's tank now?

problem: How many more books sit on the top shelf than on the bottom one? Mrs. Osei, who looks after 2 reading corners, counts 24 books on the bottom shelf and 39 on the top.
follow_up_questions: She moves 9 books from the top shelf down to the bottom shelf. How many books are on the bottom shelf now?

problem: During the quiz bowl, Freya answered 16 questions correctly and Tariq answered 11. What was the pair's total?
follow_up_questions: Their team got 52 questions right in all. How many did the other team members answer correctly?
The rival team got 47 right. By how many questions did Freya's team win?

problem: How many runs did Odette and Ravi score between them in the cricket match, if Odette made 16 and Ravi made 11?
follow_up_questions: The whole side finished on 52 runs. How many runs came from the other players?
Their opponents managed 47 runs. What was the winning margin?

problem: The cinema had 41 people watching the film, and 37 of them walked out when it ended. How many people are still in their seats?
How many birds are left on the wire? There were 41 sparrows sitting on it until a truck rumbled by and 37 flew off.
A baker made 46 cupcakes, and 9 of them have sprinkles on top. How many cupcakes have no sprinkles?
follow_up_questions: She puts 2 candles on each cupcake without sprinkles. How many candles does she use?

problem: The harbour has 46 boats tied up. Only 9 of them carry a sail. Find the number of boats without a sail.
follow_up_questions: Every boat without a sail is tied up with 2 ropes. How many ropes is that?

problem: A museum charges 7 dollars for each child. How much do 28 children from a summer camp pay to get in?
follow_up_questions: Two camp leaders come along too, paying 12 dollars each. What is the cost for the whole group?
The museum gives a 20 dollar group discount. What does the camp really pay?
The campers belong to 4 cabins, and each cabin pays an equal share. What does one cabin pay?

problem: What would a club sending 28 children pay, if swimming lessons cost 7 dollars per child?
follow_up_questions: Two coaches also swim, at 12 dollars a person. How much is the bill for everyone?
The pool knocks 20 dollars off the bill for clubs. What is the final bill?
The club splits that amount equally among 4 teams. What is each team's part?

problem: A bakery packs its bagels a dozen to a box. It made 72 bagels this morning. How many boxes does it fill?
follow_up_questions: Each box sells for 9 dollars. How much money does the bakery get for all the boxes?

problem: How many cartons are needed for 72 eggs at the farm stand, if each carton holds a dozen?
follow_up_questions: The farmer charges 9 dollars a carton. What will all the cartons sell for?

problem: Of the 60 dollars Mei spent on art supplies, 35 dollars went on paint and the rest on brushes. How much did the brushes cost?
follow_up_questions: For next term she needs twice as many brushes. What will they cost?
She has a budget of 80 dollars. How much of it is left after buying those brushes?

problem: What did the seeds cost? A gardener spent 60 dollars on soil and seeds, and 35 dollars of that went on soil.
follow_up_questions: Next spring she wants twice as many seeds. How much will those cost?
She keeps 80 dollars in her garden jar. How much remains in the jar after she buys them?

problem: There were 50 apples on the tree in Yusuf's yard until a storm knocked 20 of them down. How many apples are still hanging on the tree?
How many paper cranes were left undamaged? Lena had folded 50 of them for the festival, but rain soaked 20.
Benedikt picked out a wooden puzzle costing 30 dollars and a kite costing 20 dollars at the toy shop. What was his total bill?
follow_up_questions: He came with 90 dollars. How much money is left in his pocket?

problem: What did Sakura spend at the bookshop on a 30 dollar atlas and a 20 dollar storybook?
follow_up_questions: Her wallet held 90 dollars when she walked in. How much is in it now?

problem: A theatre has 80 seats. 50 of them are on the main floor and the rest are in the balcony. The curtains are deep red velvet. How many seats are in the balcony?
How many trays are on the dessert table? The caterer brought 80 trays and set 50 on the main buffet; every other tray went to the dessert table. The guests loved the lemon tart.
A cycling route around the lake is 24 kilometres. Jana has pedalled 15 kilometres so far. How far does she still have to cycle?
follow_up_questions: She rides the rest at 3 kilometres an hour because of the hills. How many hours does it take?
Next weekend she cycles the full route twice. How many kilometres is that?

problem: How many more kilometres must the canoe club paddle? Their river trip is 24 kilometres long, and they have done 15 kilometres.
follow_up_questions: They paddle the remaining part at 3 kilometres an hour. How long will that take in hours?
The next day they paddle the whole trip back upstream. What distance do they cover over both days?

problem: In the greenhouse, a fern reaches 25 centimetres while the palm next to it reaches 70 centimetres. By how many centimetres is the palm taller?
follow_up_questions: The fern grows 9 centimetres a week. In how many weeks will it be as tall as the palm is now?

problem: Kemal's block tower is 70 centimetres tall. How much taller is it than his sister's tower of 25 centimetres?
follow_up_questions: His sister adds 9 centimetres of blocks every day. How many days will it take her tower to reach the height Kemal's tower has now?

problem: Pedro has 53 crayons and puts them in boxes of 12 until he can't fill another box. How many crayons are left over?
follow_up_questions: How many full boxes does he make?

problem: A café baked 53 muffins. Trays hold 12 muffins each, and the cook fills every tray she can. How many muffins don't fit on a full tray?
follow_up_questions: How many trays are completely full?

problem: A gardener planted 9 rows of tulips with 12 tulips in each row, and then 5 more tulips by the gate. How many tulips did she plant?
follow_up_questions: She picks 98 tulips for the spring market. How many are still in the garden?

problem: How many pencils does the school shop have? There are 9 boxes holding 12 pencils each, plus 5 loose pencils in a cup.
follow_up_questions: Pupils buy 98 pencils in the first week. How many pencils remain?

problem: Each child at the sleepover needs exactly one sleeping bag, and the family owns 9 sleeping bags. How many children can sleep over?
follow_up_questions: 14 children want to come. How many will have to bring their own sleeping bag?

problem: How many dogs can wear a raincoat on the walk? Dana has 9 raincoats, and each dog wears one.
follow_up_questions: Her dog-walking group has 14 dogs. How many dogs are left without a raincoat?

problem: In the dance show, 11 dancers each wear 2 bracelets. How many bracelets are being worn?
follow_up_questions: A second group of dancers just as big joins them, so both groups are on stage. How many bracelets are there now?
After the show, 6 bracelets are found on the stage floor. How many went home with the dancers?

problem: How many gloves are needed if each of the 11 children on a ski trip wears 2 gloves?
follow_up_questions: A second bus with the same number of children arrives, so there are two groups. How many gloves are there for both groups?
At the end of the day, 6 gloves are left in the lodge. How many gloves leave with the children?

problem: A choir teacher divides 18 singers into 2 equal groups. How many singers are in each group?
follow_up_questions: In each group, 5 singers sing solos. How many singers in each group do not sing a solo?
How many singers without solos are there across both groups?
Then 3 of those singers go home with a cold. How many singers without solos are left?

problem: How many children are on each side when 18 children are split fairly into 2 tug-of-war teams?
follow_up_questions: Each team puts 5 children at the front of the rope. How many children on each team stand behind them?
Counting both teams, how many children stand behind the front ones?
Then 3 of those children leave to get water. How many of them are still there?

problem: Grandma shares 14 cookies equally between her 2 grandsons. How many cookies does each grandson get?
follow_up_questions: One grandson is then handed 5 more cookies by his aunt. How many cookies does he have now?

problem: How many marbles does each twin get if their dad shares 14 marbles evenly between the 2 of them?
follow_up_questions: One twin wins 5 more marbles at school. How many does that twin have now?

problem: There are 4 penguin pools at the zoo, and the keeper divides 32 buckets of fish fairly between them. How many buckets does one pool get?
follow_up_questions: The penguins in each pool eat 2 buckets a day. For how many days will one pool's buckets last?
How many buckets do the penguins in all the pools eat each day?

problem: How many logs does each cabin get when a camp warden splits 32 logs equally among 4 cabins?
follow_up_questions: Each cabin burns 2 logs every night. How many nights will a cabin's logs last?
How many logs do all the cabins burn together each night?

problem: Each of 9 cups on the art table gets the same number of crayons, and there are 45 crayons in all. The cups are bright orange plastic. How many crayons are in one cup?
follow_up_questions: The teacher gives 3 cups to the classroom next door. How many crayons does that classroom get?
How many crayons stay in her own classroom?
She shares those equally among 6 tables. How many crayons does each table get?

problem: How many stickers are in each packet, if a shopkeeper divides 45 stickers equally among 9 packets? The packets have shiny silver edges.
follow_up_questions: A customer buys 3 packets. How many stickers does the customer take home?
How many stickers are still in the shop?
The shopkeeper hands the rest out equally to 6 children. How many does each child receive?

problem: The camp cook grilled 42 sausages for the 6 tents and gave every tent the same number. How many sausages did each tent receive?
follow_up_questions: Each tent eats all but 2 of its sausages. How many sausages does each tent eat?
How many sausages are eaten by all the tents together?

problem: A farmer has 6 rabbits and 42 carrots. If every rabbit is given an equal share, what is each rabbit's share?
follow_up_questions: Every rabbit leaves 2 of its carrots uneaten. How many carrots does one rabbit eat?
How many carrots are eaten by the rabbits altogether?

problem: A bakery puts 8 pies on each rack. It has 56 pies to cool. How many racks does it use?
follow_up_questions: The cooling room has space for 4 racks. How many racks must stay outside it?
How many pies are on the racks outside the cooling room?
10 of those pies are sold right away. How many of them are left?

problem: How many shelves does Nadia fill if she arranges her 56 model cars 8 to a shelf?
follow_up_questions: Her glass cabinet has room for 4 shelves. How many shelves of cars won't fit in it?
Those shelves go in the hallway. How many cars are in the hallway?
She gives 10 of the hallway cars to her cousin. How many hallway cars does she have left?

problem: Yaw ties his 21 spare pencils into bundles of 3. How many bundles does he make?
follow_up_questions: He sells each bundle for 4 dollars at the school fair. How much could he make?

problem: How many bags will 21 apples fill, if Ines puts 3 apples in each bag?
follow_up_questions: A bag goes for 4 dollars at the market. How much money could all the bags bring in?

problem: Aunt Pilar is making bunting for a garden party. She has 36 metres of ribbon and cuts it into lengths of 4 metres, one for each string of flags. How many lengths does she cut?
follow_up_questions: Only 6 lengths are needed on the porch. How many lengths are left over for later?
Each length on the porch gets 5 paper flags. How many flags does she need?
Flags come in packs of 10. How many packs does she open?

problem: How many pieces of rope does a sailing teacher get when he cuts 36 metres of rope into pieces 4 metres long?
follow_up_questions: Only 6 boats are going out today, and each takes one piece. How many pieces stay in the boathouse?
Every boat going out also needs 5 clips. How many clips does he hand out?
Clips come in bags of 10. How many bags must he open?

problem: At the fair, Linnea has 40 dollars from her birthday and buys a stuffed panda for 26 dollars. How much money does she have left?
follow_up_questions: Later she spends 5 dollars on a candy apple. How much does she have now?
Her grandpa promises to double the money she has left. How much will she have then?

problem: How much money does Haruto take home from the aquarium shop? He came with 40 dollars and bought a toy whale for 26 dollars.
follow_up_questions: On the way out he pays 5 dollars for a snack. How much is left?
At home, his dad doubles whatever he still has. What does Haruto have now?

problem: A farmer keeps 14 hens in each henhouse, and today he is cleaning the two henhouses near the gate. How many hens does he have to move out first?
follow_up_questions: 9 of the hens run off into the yard. How many hens are still waiting by the henhouses?

problem: How many books must the librarian check? There are two carts by the door, and each cart holds 14 books.
follow_up_questions: She puts 9 of the books back on the shelves. How many are still on the carts?

problem: A cupcake shop packs 6 cupcakes in each box. The bakers made 72 cupcakes today. How many boxes can the shop fill?
follow_up_questions: 5 boxes are sold before noon. How many boxes are left?
A box costs 4 dollars. How much will the shop earn if it sells every remaining box?

problem: Find the number of egg trays a farmer fills from 72 eggs, when each tray holds 6 eggs.
follow_up_questions: The farmer delivers 5 trays to the corner shop. How many trays remain on the farm?
Each tray sells for 4 dollars at the market. What would the remaining trays sell for?

problem: Coach Lindqvist is running a partner race, which needs pairs of runners. There are 26 children on the field. How many pairs can be made?
follow_up_questions: There are only 8 sacks, and each pair needs one. How many pairs have to wait for a sack?

problem: How many teams of two can 26 dancers form for the waltz lesson?
follow_up_questions: The hall has room for only 8 pairs on the floor at a time. How many pairs must wait at the side?

problem: Last year 6 identical birdhouses used 30 nails. This year the club is building 8 of the same birdhouses. How many nails should they buy?
follow_up_questions: Nails come in boxes of 10. How many boxes do they need?
A box of nails costs 3 dollars. How much do the nails cost?
The club pays with a 20 dollar note. How much change comes back?

problem: How many buttons will Sofia need for 8 coats, if 6 of the same coats took 30 buttons?
follow_up_questions: Buttons are sold in cards of 10. How many cards should she buy?
Each card costs 3 dollars. What does she spend?
She pays with a 20 dollar note. What change does she get?

problem: A coach has 48 tennis balls and puts 6 in each bucket so every court gets the same. How many buckets does she fill?
follow_up_questions: Then 3 more courts open, and she fills one more bucket for each of them. How many tennis balls has she put in buckets altogether?

problem: How many plates does Chef Arjun fill when he places 6 dumplings on each plate from a batch of 48?
follow_up_questions: 3 more guests walk in, and he fills a plate with the same number for each. How many dumplings has he served in total?

problem: Tomasz has 42 stamps and wants to fill pages of his album with exactly 7 stamps each. How many pages can he fill?
How many cakes can a baker decorate if she has 42 cherries and puts 7 cherries on every cake?
Every skater at the rink rents a pair of skates. Ten skaters arrive for the evening session. How many skates are rented?
follow_up_questions: After an hour, 3 skaters give back their pairs of skates. How many skates are still out on the ice?
The skates still on the ice are later lined up on benches, 7 to a bench. How many benches are used?

problem: How many oars are in the boats? Ten rowers set out on the lake, and each one holds a pair of oars.
follow_up_questions: During a break, 3 rowers leave their pairs of oars on the jetty. How many oars are still in the boats?
The oars still in the boats are tied in bunches of 7. How many bunches are there?

problem: On a seesaw at the playground, 4 sandbags of 5 kilograms each sit on one end. One heavy box on the other end balances it exactly. How heavy is the box?
follow_up_questions: The box is swapped for bags of 10 kilograms. How many of those bags balance the seesaw?
Then 3 more of the 5 kilogram sandbags are put on the first end. What does that end weigh now?
How many kilograms must go on the other end to balance it again?

problem: What does the parcel weigh? On the post office scale, a parcel exactly balances 4 weights of 5 kilograms each.
follow_up_questions: The clerk swaps the parcel for weights of 10 kilograms. How many of these are needed to balance?
Next, 3 extra weights of 5 kilograms are added to the pan holding the small weights. How heavy is that pan now?
By how many kilograms must the other pan be increased to balance again?

problem: Large vans seat 8 children each. A school group that came to the zoo in 6 minivans, 4 children per minivan, is going home in large vans. How many large vans are needed?
follow_up_questions: Each large van also carries 2 teachers. How many teachers ride home?
How many people ride home altogether, teachers included?

problem: How many big tables did the party need after moving? The guests first sat at 6 small tables with 4 guests each, then all moved to big tables that seat 8.
follow_up_questions: Each big table got 2 waiters to serve it. How many waiters were working?
How many guests and waiters were there in all?

problem: Ms. Kowalski had arranged the desks in 3 rows of 8. For the class play she moves them into 4 equal rows instead. The classroom smells of fresh paint. How many desks are in each new row?
How many cars will park in each line? The car show had 3 lines of 8 cars, but the organiser now wants them in 4 equal lines. A brass band played near the entrance.
A plane carried 7 rows of 4 tourists to the island. They took 2 boats from the airport, with the tourists split equally. How many tourists rode in each boat?
follow_up_questions: Each of the two boats also had one captain. How many people crossed in the boats altogether?
At the dock, 9 of those people got straight into taxis. How many were still on the dock?

problem: How many campers sat in each canoe? At the campsite 7 rows of 4 campers lined up, and then they were shared equally between 2 huge canoes.
follow_up_questions: A guide sat in each of the two canoes as well. How many people were in the canoes altogether?
When they landed, 9 of them ran to the beach. How many stayed with the canoes?

problem: In the woods, Ana picked 9 mushrooms and her cousin Rui picked 6. How many mushrooms did the two of them pick?
follow_up_questions: They fry 5 mushrooms for supper. How many are left?
A neighbour gives them 4 more from her garden. How many do they have now?
They wrap the mushrooms in paper, 2 per packet. How many packets do they make?

problem: How many eggs did the twins collect from the henhouse if Leila gathered 9 and Omar gathered 6?
follow_up_questions: Their mother uses 5 eggs for a cake. How many eggs remain?
Grandpa brings 4 more eggs from his farm. How many eggs do they have now?
They store the eggs in small boxes holding 2 each. How many boxes are filled?

problem: A game of tag in the park had twelve players until 5 went home for dinner. How many players were left in the game?
follow_up_questions: Soon after, 3 of them came back out to play. How many players are in the game now?

problem: How many musicians kept playing after 5 of the twelve in the band left for a snack break?
follow_up_questions: Later, 3 of the musicians came back with sandwiches. How many musicians are playing now?

problem: In the class pet corner there are 8 goldfish and 7 guppies in the big tank. How many fish are in the tank?
follow_up_questions: The teacher adds 6 tetras. How many fish are in the tank now?
For the holidays, the fish are shared equally among 3 smaller tanks. How many go in each tank?
In one of those tanks, 2 fish hide behind a plant. How many can still be seen in that tank?

problem: What is the total number of animals in the petting pen, which has 8 lambs and 7 goats?
follow_up_questions: The farmer brings in 6 piglets. How many animals are in the pen now?
At night the animals are split equally into 3 stalls. How many animals sleep in each stall?
In one stall, 2 animals curl up under the straw and can't be seen. How many in that stall are visible?

problem: In the garden, Ivy spotted 16 butterflies. That was 4 more than her brother spotted. How many butterflies did her brother spot?
follow_up_questions: How many butterflies did they spot in all?
After lunch they spotted 9 more butterflies together. What is their total for the day?
Their grandmother once spotted 50 butterflies in a single week. How many fewer did the children spot today?

problem: How many shells did Felix collect, if his sister Rosa collected 16 shells, 4 more than Felix?
follow_up_questions: What is the number of shells they collected together?
Later they found 9 more shells between them. How many shells do they have for the whole day?
Their uncle's record is 50 shells. How many shells short of his record are they?

problem: At the market, Tunde puts 13 carrots and 9 onions into his bag. A street musician plays the violin nearby. How many vegetables are in his bag?
How many beads does Maren's necklace have? She strings 13 blue beads and then 9 white beads. Her little sister watches from the sofa.
Ollie looks out at the farm and sees 7 cows in the field. Each cow has 4 legs. How many legs are there in total?
How many wheels are in the car park if 7 cars are parked there and each car has 4 wheels?
Bongani draws 9 triangles on his poster. Each triangle has 3 sides. How many sides did he draw?
follow_up_questions: Next to them he draws 6 squares, each with 4 sides. How many sides are on the poster now?

problem: A quilt has 9 triangle patches sewn on it. What is the total number of sides on those patches, if every triangle has 3 sides?
follow_up_questions: Grandma also sews on 6 square patches with 4 sides each. How many sides do all the patches have together?

problem: The Ito family has 5 members, and all of them join a pottery class that charges 9 dollars per person. What is the family's total cost?
follow_up_questions: Two neighbours ask to join them. What would the class cost for all of them?
They have a voucher for 10 dollars off the total. What do they pay with the voucher?

problem: What does a family of 5 pay for a boat ride on the lake, at 9 dollars a person?
follow_up_questions: Two friends hop on board with them. What does the ride cost for everyone now?
The captain takes 10 dollars off because it is a holiday. How much do they pay in the end?

problem: Mrs. Abara wanted 6 small cartons of juice for the picnic, each holding 5 cups. The shop also has big jugs holding 15 cups. If she buys jugs instead, how many jugs give her the same amount of juice?
follow_up_questions: A big jug costs 9 dollars. What does she spend on the big jugs?

problem: How many big sacks of rice would give Chen the same amount as 6 small sacks? Small sacks hold 5 kilograms and big sacks hold 15 kilograms.
follow_up_questions: Each big sack costs 9 dollars. How much does Chen pay for the big sacks?

problem: There are 40 biscuits for the school fair, and Mrs. Larsen puts 8 on every plate. How many plates does she fill?
follow_up_questions: Visitors empty 3 plates in the first hour. How many plates still have biscuits?

problem: How many baskets does Kemal need to hold 40 oranges if he puts 8 oranges in each basket?
follow_up_questions: Customers buy 3 full baskets. How many baskets are left on his stall?

problem: A school orders pencils in boxes of a dozen. This term 7 boxes arrive. How many pencils is that?
follow_up_questions: By the end of the month, 39 pencils have been handed out. How many are still in the boxes?
The leftover pencils are sold to parents at 2 dollars each. How much money would that raise if they all sell?

problem: How many eggs travel to the shop when a farmer loads 7 trays holding a dozen eggs each?
follow_up_questions: The shop sells 39 eggs on the first day. How many eggs are left?
The rest go for 2 dollars each. What money comes in if they all sell?

problem: For the food drive, every box can take 9 cans. The class has collected 36 cans. A poster about the drive hangs by the door. How many boxes will they fill?
How many jars does Ruth fill with her 36 homemade cookies, putting 9 in each jar? Her kitchen smells of cinnamon.
Kiri's older sister reads twice as long as Kiri each evening, and Kiri reads for 15 minutes. Over 4 evenings, how many minutes does the sister spend reading?
follow_up_questions: How many minutes does Kiri read over those same evenings?
How many more minutes did her sister read than Kiri?

problem: Over 4 days, how many minutes does Luca spend swimming laps, if he swims twice as long each day as his cousin, who swims for 15 minutes a day?
follow_up_questions: How many minutes does his cousin swim in those same days?
By how many minutes did Luca's swimming beat his cousin's?

problem: Amaya and her 4 cousins share a tray of 30 brownies equally. How many brownies does each child get?
How many stickers does each person get, if a sheet of 30 stickers is split equally between Tobias and his 4 classmates?
Hamid and 3 friends won a science contest and shared the 48 dollar prize equally among all of them. How much did each one receive?
follow_up_questions: Hamid spends 5 dollars of his share on a book. How much of it does he still have?

problem: A relay team of Ewa and her 3 teammates won 48 dollars at sports day. What is each runner's equal share?
follow_up_questions: Ewa buys a 5 dollar water bottle with her share. How much does she have left?

problem: Paper cups are sold in sleeves of 6. The café wants exactly 54 cups for a party. How many sleeves does it buy?
follow_up_questions: One sleeve costs 7 dollars. How much will all the cups cost?

problem: How many packs of 6 tennis balls make exactly the 54 balls the club needs?
follow_up_questions: A pack is priced at 7 dollars. What will the club pay?

problem: Mrs. Tanaka hung 23 paper lanterns in the garden. During the windy evening, 8 of them blew away. How many lanterns were still hanging?
follow_up_questions: Her son takes 5 lanterns into the house. How many are left in the garden?
At the end of the night each guest takes 2 lanterns home, and none are left. How many guests took lanterns?

problem: How many cupcakes were left on the table, if Dmitri's dad set out 23 cupcakes and 8 got squashed when the dog jumped up?
follow_up_questions: Dmitri's sister carries 5 cupcakes to the neighbours. How many are on the table now?
The remaining cupcakes are shared out at 2 per guest with none left over. How many guests got cupcakes?

problem: Every curtain in the school hall needs 8 metres of cloth. The tailor has a single 32 metre roll. Her shop window is full of hats. How many curtains can she make?
How many window boxes can Mr. Brennan edge with a 32 metre strip of trim, if each box needs 8 metres? A cat dozes on the sunny sill.
When a bus honked, some pigeons flew up from the square onto the roofs. Before that there had been 38 pigeons pecking at crumbs; now 17 are left in the square. How many pigeons flew up?
follow_up_questions: Later, 7 of the pigeons on the roofs fly back down. How many pigeons are in the square now?
Half of the pigeons in the square tuck in their heads and doze. How many are dozing?

problem: How many children went inside when the bell rang? There were 38 children on the playground, and afterwards just 17 were still outside.
follow_up_questions: Then 7 of the children who went in come back out. How many children are on the playground now?
Half of them start a game of football. How many are playing football?

problem: Lea gathered 27 acorns in the park and Jonas gathered 18. Then, under one big oak, the two of them found 9 more. What is the total number of acorns they have?
